cause.note: layer-below audit while drafting the types part design

changes.what: The footer's pointer to the types design now names 05-the-types.md; 04 is the big-picture design.
changes.why: The pointer named a file that does not exist and a number the big picture now occupies; a reader following it found nothing. Found by the layer-below audit rule 111 requires of every review.

cause.note: operator's observation that embedded revision history bloats a document and skews later model readers

changes.what: Restructured to read as a first version: revision paragraphs, section markers, and 'the first draft said' prose removed from the body; the history moved to this changelog.
changes.why: Embedded revision notes take up space and repeat the content they annotate, tilting a later reader — especially a model — toward what changed rather than what is. This is the shape proposed as rule 91.

cause.note: conversation with the operator while the second review was open

changes.what: History becomes a rule: 'History is a lookup' (rule 90). Every governing thing is versioned by construction; supersedes and approvedIn join the common facts, generated from git.
changes.why: A governed thing whose history is not recorded by construction can drift silently.

changes.what: The rules themselves become register kind 13, with parent and mergedInto declared and children, siblings, enforcedBy derived; the rule book becomes a rendering of that kind.
changes.why: Writing the rule tree's edges down turns 'is the rule book a tree?' from a reading exercise into a build check.

changes.what: reversible replaces undoable as the allowed value on the reversibility field.
changes.why: One vocabulary, matching the rule's word (irreversible); undoable was a needless second vocabulary.

changes.what: Added the runaway rule: a profile describes the worst case the code can produce before anyone can stop it, so a failure that takes a channel away (a flood, an unbounded notifier) is control, therefore critical.
changes.why: The first draft's 'merely bothers' would have let a flood through on the strength of its single-message case.

changes.what: Operator and user reframed around principals and standing.
changes.why: The first draft defined operator as 'the one verified person' and also said 'every operator is a user'; the contradiction resolves once operator is a standing a verified person holds in a scope.

changes.what: The terms registry becomes a real register kind (12) rather than a sentence.
changes.why: The first draft said each definition 'is itself a register entry (kind: term)'; the review asked whether that was a real structure or a figure of speech — it was a figure of speech.

changes.what: Both userFacing and significance on features become derived columns.
changes.why: The first draft named only one of them; a correction to step two (the register).

changes.what: First draft of the glossary: derive irreversible, user-facing, critical and significant from a declared profile; define the nouns the register's required facts lean on; four questions for the operator.
changes.why: Step one, finding 4: a rule that uses an undefined load-bearing term is not yet a rule.
